newsitem.title: ITALY: No sign yet of Italy recovery - Fiat chairman.
newsitem.headline: No sign yet of Italy recovery - Fiat chairman.

text.p: Cesare Romiti, chairman of industrial giant Fiat, said he saw no signs yet of an Italian upturn and that a fall in inflation was mainly due to the economy's weakness.
"The country still has a desperate need of growth and the economy does not seem to show signs of awakening," he said in an interview with Turin daily La Stampa.

"The record fall in prices is certainly due to the anti-inflationist policy of the government and the rigour of the Bank of Italy, but it cannot be denied that it is also linked to the weakness of the economy," Romiti said.
Italian CPI inflation has been slashed to an estimated 1.5 percent year-on-year in May from 4.3 percent a year ago.
Romiti said the only sector where a recovery was noticeable was the auto sector, which has benefited from a government sponsored bonus incentive scheme to swap old cars for new.
Fiat Auto, which dominates the domestic car market, has seen sales jump since the scheme was introduced in January.

"These forms of support should be judged by their results and indeed could be extended to other sectors, like household electrical appliances, motorbikes or the building industry," Romiti added. -- Milan newsroom +392 66129589
